summary:
We built SearchX, an educational web app that helps high schoolers learn astrophysics for exploring real telescope data on an interactive sky map.  

You can search by object name, catalog ID, or coordinates, browse the object library, switch between visible light and infrared, and save favourite objects or share a sky view. You can also play observations from different dates, like the Barnard’s Star time-lapse, review possible changes with SIEVE, and follow links to the original data.

We also developed object-specific quizzes,and side-by-side comparisons. We wanted students and anyone curious about astronomy to be able to go from looking up an object to seeing how astronomers use observations to tell what changed and what’s still uncertain.
details:
SearchX is a web app that lets people explore real telescope observations without needing to install astronomy software. Users can look up an object by name, catalog ID, or coordinates, then switch between visible-light and infrared views of the same area. They can play observations from different dates, save favourite objects, share sky views, and open the original data. We also quizzes about individual objects and side-by-side comparisons with sourced reports that can be saved as PDF or Markdown.

Our creative approach was to put a clear example of change next to a case where the evidence is less certain. In the Barnard’s Star time-lapse, users can see the star move against the background stars. In the SIEVE review, they can examine an uncertain case and learn why differences in wavelength or image alignment matter. We want students to get practice looking at real evidence, checking its source, and deciding what they can reasonably conclude from it.

We built SearchX with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Node.js, using Aladin Lite for the interactive map. The imagery comes from the Digitized Sky Survey, SPHEREx, and NEOWISE. Our team considered how easily a first-time user could find an object, how the controls would work on phones, and how to show uncertainty and link back to the data without making the app hard to use. We tested the experience on desktop, laptop, and mobile screen sizes.
projectRefs: Canadian Astronomy Data Centre (CADC), via CANFAR
